You are working in the Ligra graph-processing framework at /workspace.
The framework (/workspace/ligra/*.h) is COMPLETE and already implements
vertexSubset, edgeMap/edgeMapData/edgeMapDense/edgeMapDenseForward/edgeMapSparse/
edgeMapSparse_no_filter, edgeMapFilter, packEdges, vertexMap, vertexFilter,
vertexFilter2 and parallel_main. DO NOT MODIFY ANY FILE under /workspace/ligra/,
and DO NOT MODIFY /workspace/apps/Makefile or any other app's .C file.
Your ONLY writable file is the single .C file named in your task.

Build & run (apps/ has symlinks to ../ligra/*.h already):
  cd /workspace/apps && make <AppName>
Compiler line: g++ -std=c++14 -O3 -DBYTERLE -o <App> <App>.C

CRITICAL framework facts (verify by reading the headers before coding):
* In the default build, parallel.h maps parallel_for -> plain `for` (single
  threaded). Code must still be written with correct atomics (CAS/writeMin/
  writeAdd) as upstream Ligra does, but execution is deterministic.
* Types: uintE/intE (32-bit by default), uintT/intT, UINT_E_MAX, INT_E_MAX.
* ligra/utils.h provides: CAS, writeMin, writeAdd, hashInt, newA, granular_for,
  sequence::plusReduce, sequence::plusScan, pbbs::* . There is NO writeOr --
  if you need atomic bitwise-or, define it locally in your .C file.
* edgeMap signature:
    edgeMap(graph<vertex>& GA, VS& vs, F f, intT threshold = -1, const flags& fl = 0)
  flags available: no_output, pack_edges, sparse_no_filter, dense_forward,
  dense_parallel, remove_duplicates, no_dense, edge_parallel.
  threshold -1 means "use GA.m/20".
* The user struct F passed to edgeMap must provide update(s,d),
  updateAtomic(s,d) and cond(d). For WEIGHTED apps the signatures are
  update(s,d,weight) / updateAtomic(s,d,weight).
* vertexMap(VS& V, F f) calls f(v) for a plain vertexSubset.
* vertexFilter(vertexSubset V, F filter) -> dense-based result.
  vertexFilter2(...) -> sparse-based result.
* vertexSubset constructors: vertexSubset(n) empty; vertexSubset(n, v) single
  vertex; vertexSubset(n, m, uintE* sparseArray); vertexSubset(n, m, bool* dense).
  Methods: isEmpty(), numNonzeros(), numRows(), toSparse(), toDense(), del(),
  vtx(i), isIn(v), dense().
* cond_true(d) is provided for "always true" cond functions.
* Every app is a template function:
    template <class vertex> void Compute(graph<vertex>& GA, commandLine P) {...}
  It MUST be a template over vertex, because parallel_main instantiates it for
  symmetricVertex, asymmetricVertex, compressedSymmetricVertex and
  compressedAsymmetricVertex. Therefore ONLY use the vertex methods that also
  exist on compressed vertices: getOutDegree(), getInDegree(),
  decodeOutNgh / decodeInNghBreakEarly / decodeOutNghSparse /
  decodeOutNghSparseSeq / countOutNgh / packOutNgh / copyOutNgh.
  *** DO NOT call getOutNeighbor(j) / getOutNeighbors() / getInNeighbor(j) in an
  app *** -- those do not exist on compressed vertices and the app must keep
  compiling once Ligra+ compressed vertices are implemented. If you need the
  neighbour list, materialize it with copyOutNgh (see apps/Triangle.C for the
  exact idiom) or use countOutNgh with a predicate.
* Read /workspace/apps/BFS.C, /workspace/apps/PageRank.C and
  /workspace/apps/Triangle.C first -- match their style, comment density and
  the 23-line MIT licence header they carry.
* /workspace/tutorial/*.C contains SKELETONS with "//FILL IN" markers showing
  the intended structure of some apps. Use them as structural hints only.

Inputs: ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 (symmetric, unweighted, n=128 m=708,
run with -s) and ../inputs/rMatGraph_WJ_5_100 (symmetric, WEIGHTED, run with -s).

Always finish by actually building and running your app and confirming the
output is sane. Report exactly what you ran and what it printed.


You are an INDEPENDENT VERIFIER for /workspace/apps/BellmanFord.C, which another agent just wrote.

The spec it was given was:
Implement /workspace/apps/BellmanFord.C -- single-source shortest paths
(Bellman-Ford) on a WEIGHTED graph.
* First line of the file (before including ligra.h) must be: #define WEIGHTED 1
* Struct BF_F holds intE* ShortestPathLen and int* Visited.
  - update(s,d,edgeLen): newDist = ShortestPathLen[s]+edgeLen; if it improves
    ShortestPathLen[d], store it, and return 1 only the first time d is added
    this round (guard with Visited[d]).
  - updateAtomic(s,d,edgeLen): return (writeMin(&ShortestPathLen[d],newDist) &&
    CAS(&Visited[d],0,1)).
  - cond(d): cond_true(d).
* A BF_Vertex_F functor resets Visited[i]=0, applied with vertexMap to the
  output frontier each round.
* Compute: source from P.getOptionLongValue("-r",0). ShortestPathLen init to
  INT_E_MAX, source 0. Loop while frontier non-empty; if round == n report a
  negative weight cycle and break. Use edgeMap(...,GA.m/20,dense_forward).
* Report: "BellmanFord rounds: <N>" and the number of reachable vertices as
  "BellmanFord reachable: <N>" (vertices with ShortestPathLen != INT_E_MAX),
  and "BellmanFord sum: <N>" = sum of finite distances.
* Run it: ./BellmanFord -r 0 -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_WJ_5_100

Its report was:
**File:** `/workspace/apps/BellmanFord.C` (only file created; `apps/Makefile` and `ligra/ligra.h` show as modified in git but were already modified in the starting snapshot — I did not touch them)

## Commands run

```
cd /workspace/apps && make BellmanFord
# g++ -std=c++14 -O3   -DBYTERLE   -o BellmanFord BellmanFord.C     (clean, no warnings/errors)

cd /workspace/apps && ./BellmanFord -r 0 -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_WJ_5_100
```

## Full stdout

```
BellmanFord rounds: 9
BellmanFord reachable: 125
BellmanFord sum: 1291
BellmanFord rounds: 9
BellmanFord reachable: 125
BellmanFord sum: 1291
Running time : 2e-05
```

(Two blocks because `parallel_main` calls `Compute` once untimed then `-rounds 1` more.)

## Implementation

- Line 1 is `#define WEIGHTED 1`, then the 23-line MIT header, then `#include "ligra.h"`.
- `BF_F{intE* ShortestPathLen; int* Visited;}` with `update(s,d,edgeLen)` (stores improvement, returns 1 only on the first improvement per round, guarded by `Visited[d]`), `updateAtomic` = `writeMin(&ShortestPathLen[d],newDist) && CAS(&Visited[d],0,1)`, `cond(d) = cond_true(d)`.
- `BF_Vertex_F` resets `Visited[i]=0`, applied via `vertexMap(output, ...)` each round.
- `edgeMap(GA, Frontier, BF_F(...), GA.m/20, dense_forward)`; loop breaks with a negative-weight-cycle message when `round == n`.
- Uses only `getOutDegree`/decode-based paths — `grep` for `getOutNeighbor|getOutNeighbors|getInNeighbor` in the file returns 0 hits, so it stays compilable against compressed vertices.

## Verification beyond the required run

1. **Independent Python Dijkstra** on `rMatGraph_WJ_5_100` (parsed offsets/edges/weights directly): `reachable 125, sum 1291`, and a reference frontier-based Bellman-Ford gives `rounds 9` and a distance vector identical to Dijkstra's. Exact match with the app.
2. **Alternate sources** `-r 1`, `-r 5`, `-r 100` → `(1, 0, 1 round)`, `(1, 0, 1 round)`, `(125, 1155, 8 rounds)`; all three match Python Dijkstra exactly. Vertices 1 and 5 are isolated in this input, hence reachable=1.
3. **Negative-cycle branch** exercised with a throwaway 4-vertex graph in `/tmp` containing a reachable −2 cycle: printed `BellmanFord negative weight cycle` then `rounds: 4` (= n) and exited 0. Temp files deleted.
4. **Non-atomic `update()` path** — with `dense_forward` the app only ever calls `updateAtomic`, so I compiled a throwaway copy in `/tmp` with the flag changed to `0` (forcing `edgeMapDense`, which calls `update`): identical output `9 / 125 / 1291`. Both code paths agree. Temp copy deleted; the committed file keeps `dense_forward` as specified.

## Concerns

- Input weights are all in [1,7] (checked), so no overflow risk here. In general `ShortestPathLen[s] + edgeLen` is computed in `intE` (32-bit `int` by default); this is upstream Ligra's behavior, and it is safe because `dense_forward`/sparse only relax out-edges of frontier vertices, which always have finite distance — an `INT_E_MAX + w` overflow cannot occur. It would be reachable if the app were ever switched to plain dense mode with a `cond_true`, so I left the `dense_forward` flag as the task specifies.
- On the negative-cycle break I print the message and report the last-computed distances rather than clobbering the array to `-(INT_E_MAX/2)` as upstream does, so that `reachable`/`sum` stay interpretable.
- `reachable`/`sum` are computed with a sequential `for` loop (not `parallel_for`), which is intentional: it is reporting code and accumulating into a scalar would race under a real parallel build.

Your job: try to REFUTE that this app is correct and complete.
1. Read the file. Check it really implements the named algorithm (not a stub or a
   trivially-wrong shortcut), that it is `template <class vertex>`, and that it
   does NOT call getOutNeighbor/getOutNeighbors/getInNeighbor/getInNeighbors
   (those break on compressed vertices later).
2. Rebuild from scratch: cd /workspace/apps && rm -f BellmanFord && make BellmanFord
   -- it must compile with no errors. Warnings are acceptable.
3. Run it and check the printed numbers are actually right. Where feasible,
   compute the ground truth INDEPENDENTLY with a small python script over
   /workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 (or rMatGraph_WJ_5_100 for the weighted
   app) and compare. Do not trust the implementation's own claims.
4. Confirm it does not modify anything under /workspace/ligra/, the Makefile,
   or another app (check: cd /workspace && git status --short).

If you find a real defect, FIX IT in BellmanFord.C (that file only), rebuild,
rerun, and re-verify. Then report.

Return: VERDICT (PASS or FIXED or BROKEN), the ground-truth values you computed
independently, the values the app printed, and anything still wrong.

cat > /tmp/gt_bf.py <<'EOF'
import heapq, sys
INF = 2**31 - 1  # INT_E_MAX

toks = open('/workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_WJ_5_100').read().split()
assert toks[0] == 'WeightedAdjacencyGraph', toks[0]
n = int(toks[1]); m = int(toks[2])
offs = [int(x) for x in toks[3:3+n]]
tgts = [int(x) for x in toks[3+n:3+n+m]]
wts  = [int(x) for x in toks[3+n+m:3+n+2*m]]
assert len(toks) == 3+n+2*m, (len(toks), 3+n+2*m)
adj = []
for i in range(n):
    o = offs[i]; e = m if i == n-1 else offs[i+1]
    adj.append(list(zip(tgts[o:e], wts[o:e])))
print("n=%d m=%d minw=%d maxw=%d" % (n, m, min(wts), max(wts)))

def dijkstra(src):
    d = [INF]*n; d[src]=0; pq=[(0,src)]
    while pq:
        du,u = heapq.heappop(pq)
        if du > d[u]: continue
        for v,w in adj[u]:
            if du + w < d[v]:
                d[v] = du + w; heapq.heappush(pq,(d[v],v))
    return d

def ligra_sim(src, threshold_num=20):
    """Replicate exactly: dense_forward when m_frontier+outDegrees > GA.m/20,
       else sparse; both iterate Gauss-Seidel style in index / sparse order."""
    d = [INF]*n; d[src]=0
    frontier = [src]                 # sparse order as Ligra keeps it
    thresh = m // threshold_num
    rounds = 0
    while frontier:
        if rounds == n: return d, rounds, True
        outDeg = sum(len(adj[u]) for u in frontier)
        visited = [0]*n; out = []
        if len(frontier) + outDeg > thresh:
            # dense_forward: iterate i = 0..n-1 in index order
            fset = set(frontier)
            order = [i for i in range(n) if i in fset]
        else:
            order = list(frontier)   # sparse: frontier order
        for u in order:
            for v,w in adj[u]:
                nd = d[u] + w
                if nd < d[v]:
                    d[v] = nd
                    if not visited[v]:
                        visited[v] = 1; out.append(v)
        # dense_forward output is a bool array -> toSparse gives index order
        if len(frontier) + outDeg > thresh: out.sort()
        frontier = out
        rounds += 1
    return d, rounds, False

for src in [0,1,5,100,127]:
    dd = dijkstra(src)
    ds, rounds, neg = ligra_sim(src)
    reach = sum(1 for x in dd if x != INF)
    s = sum(x for x in dd if x != INF)
    agree = (dd == ds)
    print("src=%-4d dijkstra: reachable=%-4d sum=%-6d | ligra-sim rounds=%d dists_match=%s neg=%s"
          % (src, reach, s, rounds, agree, neg))
EOF
python3 /tmp/gt_bf.py

VERDICT: **PASS** — no defect found; `/workspace/apps/BellmanFord.C` was not modified by me.

## Independently computed ground truth
Parsed `/workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_WJ_5_100` directly (`WeightedAdjacencyGraph`, n=128, m=708, weights in [1,7], layout = n offsets, m targets, m weights) with my own Python script, then ran (a) Dijkstra and (b) a from-scratch simulation of Ligra's frontier loop that replicates the `m + outDegrees > GA.m/20` dense/sparse mode choice and the Gauss-Seidel in-place relaxation order:

| source | reachable | sum | rounds |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 125 | 1291 | 9 |
| 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| 5 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| 100 | 125 | 1155 | 8 |
| 127 | 125 | 1873 | 8 |

## What the app printed
`cd /workspace/apps && rm -f BellmanFord && make BellmanFord` → `g++ -std=c++14 -O3 -DBYTERLE -o BellmanFord BellmanFord.C`, exit 0, no errors or warnings.

`./BellmanFord -r 0 -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_WJ_5_100`:
```
BellmanFord rounds: 9
BellmanFord reachable: 125
BellmanFord sum: 1291
BellmanFord rounds: 9
BellmanFord reachable: 125
BellmanFord sum: 1291
Running time : 1.88e-05
```
`-r 1` → `1 / 1 / 0`; `-r 5` → `1 / 1 / 0`; `-r 100` → `8 / 125 / 1155`; `-r 127` → `8 / 125 / 1873`. Every value matches the table above exactly.

## Adversarial checks I ran (not trusting the author's claims)
1. **Full distance vector, not just the aggregate.** Compiled an instrumented copy in `/tmp` that dumps all 128 `ShortestPathLen[i]`, and compared element-wise against my Dijkstra vector: **identical for all 128 entries** (including both `INT_E_MAX` entries at vertices 1 and 5, which are genuinely isolated in this input). This rules out a sum/count coincidence.
2. **Non-atomic `update()` path.** With `dense_forward` the app only ever reaches `updateAtomic`, so `update()` was dead code in the required run. I recompiled a `/tmp` copy with the flag changed to `0` (forcing `edgeMapDense` → `decodeInNghBreakEarly` → `update`): `9 / 125 / 1291` for `-r 0`, `125 / 1155` for `-r 100`. `update()` is correct and matches upstream Ligra verbatim.
3. **Sparse-only path.** `/tmp` copy with `no_dense`: `125 / 1291` — same distances, `rounds: 10` instead of 9. The round-count difference is expected order-dependence of in-place relaxation (dense_forward's index-order sweep converges one round faster), not a bug; my simulator reproduces both counts.
4. **Negative-weight-cycle branch.** Built a 4-vertex weighted graph in `/tmp` with a reachable −20 cycle and ran the *shipped* binary on it: printed `BellmanFord negative weight cycle` then `BellmanFord rounds: 4` (= n) and exited 0. Branch is live and correctly gated.
5. **Type-width variants.** Rebuilt with `-DLONG`, `-DEDGELONG`, and both (`intE` → `long`, `INT_E_MAX` → `LONG_MAX`): compiles clean, all give `9 / 125 / 1291`. No latent width assumption in `writeMin(&ShortestPathLen[d], newDist)` / `CAS(&Visited[d],0,1)`.
6. **Compressed-vertex safety.** `grep -nE 'getOutNeighbor|getOutNeighbors|getInNeighbor|getInNeighbors' BellmanFord.C` → 0 hits (exit 1). The app touches no vertex method directly at all; it only goes through `edgeMap`/`vertexMap`, so it will keep compiling when `compressedVertex.h` is filled in.
7. **Structure.** Line 1 is `#define WEIGHTED 1` (before the 23-line MIT header and `#include "ligra.h"`), `Compute` is `template <class vertex>`, `BF_F` has the required `update`/`updateAtomic`/`cond`, `BF_Vertex_F` resets `Visited`, `edgeMap(..., GA.m/20, dense_forward)`, `Visited[d]==1` ⟺ `d ∈ output` so the `vertexMap(output, ...)` reset is complete, and the `Frontier.del(); Frontier = output;` ownership transfer has no double-free (`vertexSubsetData` has no destructor, only `del()`).

## Isolation check
`cd /workspace && git status --short` shows `M apps/Makefile` and `M ligra/ligra.h` — both were already modified in the snapshot given to me at session start, and their mtimes (00:11, 00:10) predate `apps/BellmanFord.C` (00:45), so BellmanFord did not touch them. No other app's `.C` file is modified (the other `apps/*.C` are new untracked files from sibling agents in this workflow).

## Still-open notes (not defects, no action taken)
- `/workspace/ligra/byte.h` and `/workspace/ligra/byteRLE.h` are new untracked files under `ligra/` with mtimes *after* `BellmanFord.C`. These are the Ligra+ compression headers from task #3, i.e. a different agent — not attributable to BellmanFord.C, but flagging since the "don't touch `ligra/`" rule is being bent by someone in this workflow.
- On the negative-cycle break the app reports the last-computed distances rather than clobbering the array to `-(INT_E_MAX/2)` as upstream does. The spec only said "report a negative weight cycle and break", so this is compliant; just be aware the printed `sum`/`reachable` are then meaningless-but-finite (my test printed `4 / 0`).
- `-r` is not range-checked, so `-r <n or larger>` writes out of bounds. Upstream Ligra has the identical hole and the spec doesn't ask for a guard, so I left it.
- `reachable`/`sum` use a sequential `for`, not `parallel_for`. Correct as written (a `parallel_for` accumulating into a scalar would race under a real parallel build).

Working artifacts in `/tmp/bfver` were deleted; `/workspace/apps/BellmanFord` is the clean default `make` build.
